definitions.definition: A law of physics that says in any closed system, disorder (entropy) always increases over time; things naturally fall apart unless energy is added from outside.
definitions.example: An ice cube melts in a warm room, and the water never spontaneously refreezes without a freezer.

definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; higher entropy means more chaos, less usable energy.
definitions.example: A messy bedroom has higher entropy than a tidy one; it takes work to clean it up.

definitions.definition: A system that does not exchange energy or matter with anything outside it; it is completely closed off.
definitions.example: A sealed, perfectly insulated thermos of hot coffee is nearly isolated—no heat or matter gets in or out.

definitions.definition: Negative entropy; a measure of order, structure, or information that can be used to create local order against the natural tendency toward disorder.
definitions.example: Food provides negentropy to your body, allowing you to build and repair cells instead of falling apart.

definitions.definition: In this framework, alignment with the Logos (God's order); a state of harmony and integration, opposite of chaos.
definitions.example: A well-tuned orchestra playing together has high coherence; random noise has low coherence.

definitions.definition: A Greek word meaning 'Word' or 'Reason'; in Christian theology, it refers to Jesus Christ as the divine order and logic of the universe.
definitions.example: In the Gospel of John, 'In the beginning was the Word (Logos), and the Word was with God.'

definitions.definition: A human variable representing willingness to receive grace; how open a person is to input from God.
definitions.example: Being humble and asking for help is like having high openness; refusing help is low openness.

definitions.definition: Unearned favor and help from God; in this framework, it is negentropy (order) injected from outside the human system.
definitions.example: A student who fails a test but gets a second chance from the teacher for free is receiving grace.

definitions.definition: A rapid decrease where the amount drops by a constant percentage over equal time steps; it gets smaller and smaller very fast.
definitions.example: A bouncing ball that loses half its height each bounce follows exponential decline.

definitions.definition: Exaggerated statements not meant to be taken literally, used for emphasis.
definitions.example: Saying 'I'm so hungry I could eat a horse' is hyperbole.

definitions.term: perpetual motion machine of the second kind
definitions.definition: A hypothetical machine that would reduce entropy in a closed system without any external energy input, which is impossible by the Second Law.
definitions.example: A device that cools a room without using electricity or any fuel would be a perpetual motion machine of the second kind—it can't exist.

definitions.definition: Referring to itself; a system that only looks inward and doesn't accept outside input or truth.
definitions.example: A person who says 'I am always right because I say so' is being self-referential.

definitions.definition: Loss of coherence; a system becoming disordered and isolated from its source of order.
definitions.example: A radio signal that gets staticky and loses the clear music is undergoing decoherence.

definitions.definition: A mathematical function that is zero everywhere except at a single point, where it is infinitely tall; used to model an instantaneous event.
definitions.example: A lightning strike is like a Dirac delta function—it delivers a huge burst of energy in a split second and then stops.

definitions.definition: A Calvinist doctrine that God's grace cannot be resisted when He chooses to save someone; it overcomes human will.
definitions.example: Like a strong current that sweeps a swimmer along whether they want to go or not.

definitions.definition: A branch of Christian theology based on John Calvin's teachings, emphasizing God's sovereignty and predestination.
definitions.example: Calvinists believe God chooses who will be saved, not based on human effort.

definitions.definition: A branch of Christian theology emphasizing human free will and the ability to accept or reject God's grace.
definitions.example: Arminians believe people can choose to follow God or turn away.

definitions.definition: The idea that your actions (good or bad) will eventually return to you; a closed-loop system of cause and effect.
definitions.example: If you help someone, karma says you'll be helped later; if you hurt someone, you'll be hurt.

definitions.definition: A principle stating that erasing one bit of information requires a minimum amount of energy, so information has a physical cost.
definitions.example: Deleting a file on a computer generates a tiny amount of heat because erasing information takes energy.

definitions.definition: A physical constant that relates energy to temperature; it's a tiny number used in thermodynamics equations.
definitions.example: It's like a conversion factor between the temperature of a gas and the energy of its molecules.

definitions.definition: An action that processes or changes information, considered in terms of its physical and mathematical properties.
definitions.example: Copying a file from one drive to another is an information-theoretic operation.

definitions.definition: The Christian belief that Jesus' death on the cross paid the penalty for human sin and restored the relationship between God and people.
definitions.example: Like someone paying off your huge debt so you are free and clear.

definitions.definition: The path a system follows over time as dictated by the laws of thermodynamics, especially the Second Law.
definitions.example: A hot cup of coffee cooling to room temperature follows a thermodynamic trajectory toward equilibrium.
